questions.solution:
Ozone layer is depleted by NO.

Explanation:

  1. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and nitrogen oxides (NO, NO2) are the main culprits that destroy the ozone layer.
  2. The following reaction occurs when ozone (O3) and nitric oxide (NO) interact in the stratosphere, causing ozone depletion:
    \[\ce{NO + O_3 -> NO_2 + O_2}\]
  3. This process lowers ozone concentration, which aids in the ozone layer's thinning.
  4. NO2, NO3, and N2O5 can also participate in atmospheric reactions, but NO plays the most direct role in ozone depletion.

questions.q: One dimensional nanostructure amongst the following is:
questions.solution:
Nanotubes

Explanation:

Nanotubes are one-dimensional nanostructures because they have a high aspect ratio (length is much greater than diameter), allowing electron transport and mechanical flexibility along one dimension.

questions.q:
What is atom economy?

Explain any two applications of nanomaterials.
questions.solution:
Atom economy means most of the atoms of the reactants are incorporated in the desired products and only small amounts of unwanted byproducts are formed and hence lesser problems of waste disposal.



  1. Nanoparticles can contribute to stronger, lighter, cleaner and smarter surfaces and systems. They are used in the manufacturing of scratchproof eyeglasses, transport, sunscreen, crack resistant paints and so on.
  2. Used in electronic devices. For example, Magnetoresistive Random Acess memory (MRAM).
  3. Nanotechnology plays an important role in water purification techniques. Water contains waterborne pathogens like - viruses, bacteria. 1.1 billion people are without access to an improved water supply. The provision of safe drinking water is currently high priority. Recently, cost effective filter materials coated with silver nanoparticles (AgNps) is an alternative technology. (For example: water purifier) Silver nanoparticles act as highly effective bacterial disinfectant, remove E.Coli from water.
  4. Self cleaning materials: Lotus is an example of self cleaning. The lotus plant (Nelumbo nucifera) although grows in muddy water, its leaves always appear clean. The plants' leaves are superhydrophobic. Nanostructures on lotus leaves repel water which carries dirt as it rolls off. Lotus effect is the basis of self cleaning windows.

questions.q:
What is nano material? 



Write the reaction involved in sol-gel process during hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
1. Nanomaterials are particles that have their size in the 1-100 nm range at least in one dimension.
  2. Nanomaterials are larger than single atoms but smaller than bacteria and cells.
  3. We cannot see particles of nano with the naked eye.
  4. Examples of nanomaterials include nano zymes, titanium dioxide, nanoparticles, graphene, etc.


Sols are dispersions of colloidal particles in a liquid. A gel is an interconnected, rigid network. A sol-gel process is based on inorganic polymerisation reactions, which are widely employed to prepare oxide materials.

The reaction involved in the sol-gel process is

\[\ce{\underset{(Metal alkoxide)}{MOR} + H2O -> MOH + ROH}\] (Hydrolysis) (Metal alkoxide)

\[\ce{MOH + ROH -> M-O-M + ROH}\] (Condensation)

  • M represents a metal atom (such as Si, Ti, etc.),
  • OROR is an alkoxide group, and
  • ROHROH is the resulting alcohol.

questions.q:
Define Green chemistry.



Write any three advantages of nanoparticles and nanotechnology.
questions.solution:
Green Chemistry is the use of chemistry for pollution prevention by environmentally conscious design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances.



  1. Revolution in electronics and computing.
  2. Energy sector:
    a. Nanotechnology will make solar power more economical.
    b. Energy storage devices will become more efficient.
  3. Medical field:
    a. Manufacturing of smart drugs helps cure faster and without side effects.
    b. Curing of life-threatening diseases like cancer and diabetes.

questions.q:
Define Green chemistry.



Write two disadvantages of nanotechnology.
questions.solution:
Green Chemistry is the use of chemistry for pollution prevention by environmentally conscious design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances.



Disadvantages of Nanotechnology:

  1. It has increased pollution, including air pollution (nano pollution).
  2. Nanoparticles can harm the lungs. Particulate matter inhaled can be deposited throughout the human respiratory system and then in the lungs.
